 Judgment
Dated this the 2nd day of July, 2025 The petitioner is engaged in the distribution of Pepsi Cola in Kollam District in the name and style 'NEF' and obtained licenses from the statutory authorities.
The petitioner has been conducting the business for the last twenty five years and he has a good reputation in the said business.
For the purpose of business, the petitioner started a godown at Neeravil, Kollam at KMC 8/1596 in Ward No.8 of Kollam Corporation.

2. The petitioner states that respondents 6 and 7 and their associates are obstructing the loading and unloading work carried out in the godown of the petitioner situated at Neeravil within the limits of Kollam Corporation.
Respondents 6 and 7 are the local leaders of a Trade Union of unattached loading and unloading workers.
The loading and unloading work in the godown of the petitioner is being carried on by three workers of the petitioner.
These workers are permanent 2025:KER:48140 employees of the petitioner attached to his business concern.
The petitioner submitted application for Labour Card / registration for his permanent workers before the 5 th respondent and the applications are still pending consideration.

sentences.text: The petitioner states that there is no such Unit in Neeravil as claimed by respondents 6 and 7.
They are not registered members under 4th respondent-Board.

Things being so, on 03.06.2025,
respondents 6 and 7 and some of their henchmen came to the business premises of the petitioner situated in building No.KMC 8/1596 in Neeravil, Kollam and insisted the petitioner that loading and unloading work in the godown shall be entrusted to them.

When the petitioner declined to accept their demand, they insisted that if they are not engaged, they should be paid wages for the work carried on through by the permanent employees of the petitioner.
4. The petitioner states that finding no other way, he paid money to respondents 6 and 7 and their henchmen as gawking wages (nokku coolie) without doing any work.
On the 2025:KER:48140 same day, the petitioner gave a complaint to the 3 rd respondent- Station House Officer, but the 3rd respondent turned a Nelson eye.

Again, on 18.06.2025, when the permanent employees of the petitioner attempted to unload the soft drinks brought to the godown in a van, respondents 6 and 7 along with their henchmen, illegally trespassed into the godown and obstructed the unloading and manhandled the petitioner and his employees, contends the petitioner.
5. I have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel representing the 4 th respondent.
I have also heard the learned Government Pleader representing respondents 1 to 3 and 5.

Though notice was served by special messenger on respondents 6 and 7,
there is no representation for respondents 6 and 7.
6.
The petitioner states that the loading and unloading activities in his business concern are obstructed by respondents 6 and 7.

Standing Counsel representing the Kerala Headload Workers Welfare Board would submit that the 2025:KER:48140 petitioner's establishment is not in an area where the Kerala Headload Workers (Regulation of Employment and Welfare) Scheme is made operational.

entities.text: Kerala Headload Workers (Regulation of Employment and Welfare) Scheme
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If that be so, the petitioner will have a right to engage his own workers, or workers of his choice, for loading and unloading activities.
Respondents 6 and 7 cannot claim, as of right, any superior right for loading and unloading work.

In such circumstances, the writ petition is disposed of directing the 3rd respondent to give adequate protection to the petitioner to carry out loading and unloading work in his establishment by engaging workers of his choice.
